0.title: The hermeneutic keys
0.kicker: Daniel 1 complete · year-day companions in the dock
0.jumpLabel: Year-day and the giving of the king

loadBearing.plain: This is a date, not a dream. In Jehoiakim’s third year (about 605 B.C.), Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon attacked Jerusalem and took the first captives.

links.because: Jeremiah had already said Judah would serve Babylon seventy years. Daniel 1:1 is the start of that exile, not a one-off raid.
The history book records the same first submission of Jehoiakim to Babylon. Two witnesses, one year.

loadBearing.sitting: The book opens on a real siege. Later kingdoms must sit on this dated world, not on a floating riddle.

loadBearing.plain: The key verb is gave. Babylon’s army marched, but the Lord handed Jehoiakim and the temple vessels over. Heaven is writing the story.

links.because: The same God later tells Nebuchadnezzar, “the God of heaven hath given thee a kingdom,” and names him the head of gold.
Jeremiah already called Nebuchadnezzar God’s servant over the nations. Daniel 1:2 is that claim in one word: gave.

loadBearing.sitting: If Heaven gave the first king away, Heaven also times every kingdom that follows.

loadBearing.plain: Israel’s spies searched Canaan for forty ordinary days. God then sentenced the nation to forty ordinary years: “each day for a year.” He is mapping counted days onto counted years.

links.because: God says the same sentence again to Ezekiel in exile: “I have appointed thee each day for a year.” Two stories, one scale.
Gabriel’s seventy weeks are 490 units. That cannot be 490 ordinary days and still hold a rebuilt city and the cross. Those weeks use this day-for-year scale.

loadBearing.sitting: God taught the scale himself, long before Daniel. Later vision-days can stand for years because this appointment already exists.

loadBearing.plain: God has Ezekiel lie on his side forty days for Judah, then explains the theatre: each of those body-days stands for a year of the nation’s sin.

links.because: Same words, earlier story — the wilderness. Ezekiel is not inventing a secret code.
The 2,300 evenings-mornings sit on this same ruler: a numbered day-unit that may mean a year.

loadBearing.sitting: Ezekiel is already in exile, in Daniel’s world. The same Lord who numbered Ezekiel’s body-days later numbers Daniel’s visions.

1.title: Daniel 1
1.kicker: Hebrew · the court school at Babylon, 605 B.C.
1.jumpLabel: The Lord gave the king · the purpose of heart

loadBearing.plain: Temple cups from Jerusalem are carried into the house of a Babylonian god. They are still holy things, now sitting in the wrong house.

links.because: Chapter 5 will bring those same cups to Belshazzar’s feast. The night gold falls begins with this first theft.

loadBearing.sitting: Watch the vessels. The book will bring them back on the night the gold kingdom ends.

loadBearing.plain: Daniel decides in his heart not to eat the king’s rich food or drink his wine. The line is worship, not a modern diet fad.

links.because: Israel already had a law that separated clean animals from unclean. The royal table mixed that line.
Daniel asks for zeroim — seeds, plants, water. That is the older food of Genesis, not the meat offered to Marduk.

loadBearing.sitting: He will wear a Babylonian name and learn the language. He will not join the king’s table as worship.

loadBearing.plain: Moses already told Israel how to tell clean food from unclean food. Daniel is using that law, not inventing a new rule.

links.because: That is why “defile” is the right word. The king’s meat had crossed a line God had already drawn.
The ten-day test on vegetables and water is how Daniel keeps that old line without quitting his job.

loadBearing.sitting: The first stand is at a plate. Identity is tested before any vision is given.

loadBearing.plain: God gives these four youths learning and skill, and to Daniel he gives understanding in visions. The gift comes before the first dream.

links.because: The secret of Nebuchadnezzar’s dream is revealed in a night vision — the gift of 1:17 going to work.
Later beasts come in a dream as well. Chapter 1 already told you Daniel can receive what Heaven shows.

loadBearing.sitting: Wisdom is given first. The later visions rest on this gift, not on Babylonian magic.

loadBearing.plain: Daniel is still there when Cyrus the Persian comes. He outlives the gold kingdom.

links.because: Babylon falls in a night; Darius the Mede receives the kingdom. Daniel is still on the payroll.
Daniel prospers in the reign of Darius and in the reign of Cyrus. The first chapter already reached the silver.

loadBearing.sitting: The book’s first page already looks past Babylon. The chain will not stop at gold.

2.title: Daniel 2
2.kicker: Hebrew 1–4a · Aramaic from 4b · the metallic image, 603 B.C.

loadBearing.plain: Daniel tells the king there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and this dream is about what will happen in the latter days — real future history.

links.because: The secret was given to Daniel in a night vision after prayer, not by the court magicians.
Even Nebuchadnezzar admits Daniel’s God is a God of gods who reveals secrets. The dream is not flattery.

loadBearing.sitting: Court magic cannot steal what Heaven shows. The statue is a map of kingdoms, not a compliment.

loadBearing.plain: God names the first metal for you: “Thou art this head of gold.” Babylon is the starting point. Later metals cannot restart the statue in another century.

links.because: Jeremiah already said God gave the beasts of the field into Nebuchadnezzar’s hand — the same grant Daniel reads onto the golden head.
Chapter 7 will draw the same first kingdom as a lion. Gold and lion are one empire, two pictures.

loadBearing.sitting: Only the head is named here. Walk “after… after… after” from this verse. Do not invent a new head of gold.

loadBearing.plain: Long before the dream, Jeremiah said God had given Nebuchadnezzar the nations and even the beasts of the field.

links.because: Daniel uses that same grant: the God of heaven gave the king a kingdom, and that is why he is the head of gold.
The first page already said the Lord gave Jehoiakim into this king’s hand. Jeremiah and Daniel agree: Heaven handed power over.

loadBearing.sitting: Daniel is not guessing. He is reading Babylon the way Jeremiah already named it.

loadBearing.plain: The last part of the statue is iron mixed with clay. Rulers will try to glue the pieces together (even by marriage), but they will not stick.

links.because: The feet and toes are that mixture: partly strong, partly broken. This is divided Europe after Rome, not a fifth world-empire of one metal.
Chapter 7 will show the same stage as ten horns — many kings where one iron beast used to be.

loadBearing.sitting: The last metal is a mixture. Do not look for one more gold head. Look for kingdoms that will not cleave.

loadBearing.plain: In the days of those divided kings, God sets up a kingdom that never ends. It does not join the statue. It breaks it.

links.because: The same forever-kingdom is given to one like a son of man. Chapter 2’s stone and chapter 7’s son of man are one hope.
The stone cut without hands strikes the feet, then fills the earth. That is arrival, not a repair kit.

loadBearing.sitting: The stone does not patch Babylon or Rome. It ends the metals and stands forever.

3.title: Daniel 3
3.jumpLabel: The counterfeit image and the fourth figure

loadBearing.plain: Nebuchadnezzar builds a huge image made entirely of gold — no silver, bronze, or iron. He is answering last night’s dream with a public “no.”

links.because: The dream-statue had four metals. An all-gold image erases the other three.
God said only the head is gold. This statue claims the whole body will stay Babylon forever.

loadBearing.sitting: Dura is not interior design. It is a counter-creed: Babylon will not be replaced.

loadBearing.plain: The rule is simple and cruel: when the music plays, bow, or be thrown into the furnace.

links.because: The signal is civic music. Worship is being made into a two-second public habit.
A later image also kills those who will not worship. Dura is the rehearsal of that pattern.

loadBearing.sitting: Forced worship always arrives as a small civic bow before it arrives as a furnace.

loadBearing.plain: John sees an image that is given power to kill whoever will not worship it. That is Dura written on a larger stage.

links.because: Same structure: an image, a command to worship, death for refusal.
The little horn also presses saints and changes times and laws. The pattern is religious force, not only a Babylonian night.

loadBearing.sitting: Dura is the pattern, not a closed antique. Learn the bow here so you can name it later.

loadBearing.plain: The three men say God can save them — and if he does not, they still will not serve the image. Loyalty is not a bargain for rescue.

links.because: The second commandment already forbade making an image and bowing to it. They are keeping that word.
The apostles later say the same limit: we ought to obey God rather than men.

loadBearing.sitting: “But if not” is the sitting’s sentence. Allegiance does not wait to see whether the fire is cooled.

loadBearing.plain: The king sees four men walking in the fire, unbound, and the fourth looks like a son of the gods. God is in the furnace with them.

links.because: Nebuchadnezzar himself admits God sent his angel and delivered his servants who trusted him.
Isaiah already promised: when you walk through the fire, you shall not be burned. Presence, not always prevention.

loadBearing.sitting: Deliverance here is God walking in the heat, not a promise that the heat will never be lit.

4.title: Daniel 4
4.jumpLabel: The watcher, the stump, and the Most High

loadBearing.plain: Heaven states the lesson of the chapter: the Most High rules in the kingdom of men and gives it to whom he will. Kings are trustees, not owners.

links.because: Chapter 2 already said God removes kings and sets up kings. Chapter 4 makes one king live that sentence.
The same words are repeated when the sentence falls. The chapter exists to teach this one truth about thrones.

loadBearing.sitting: The gold head is on loan. Write 4:17 before you watch the boast on the roof.

loadBearing.plain: On the palace roof the king says, “Is not this great Babylon that I have built?” He credits himself for what Heaven gave.

links.because: Belshazzar will know this story and still lift himself up. Chapter 5 is what happens when a grandson ignores 4:30.
The older boast is “I will ascend.” Nebuchadnezzar’s “I have built” is the same pride in civic clothes.

loadBearing.sitting: The sentence falls while the boast is still in the mouth. Pride is the charge; the field is the sentence.

loadBearing.plain: After seven ordinary years as a beast, the king lifts his eyes to heaven and his mind comes back. Sanity returns with worship.

links.because: He publishes the lesson: those who walk in pride God is able to abase. The chapter ends as a decree of praise.
The lion is given a man’s heart after its wings are plucked — chapter 4 restaged as a beast. These “seven times” are a man’s years, not 2,520 prophetic years.

loadBearing.sitting: A mind that can praise again is the prize. The stump was banded so Babylon could still stand while the king learned.

5.title: Daniel 5
5.kicker: Aramaic · the night the river dropped, 539 B.C.

loadBearing.plain: Fingers write on the plaster while the feast is still loud. The king’s knees fail because he knows this is judgment, not a trick of the wine.

links.because: Those cups left Jerusalem in the first chapter. The feast is drinking from what belongs to Israel’s God.
They praised gods of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone with Yahweh’s vessels. That is the charge the hand answers.

loadBearing.sitting: Sacrilege is dated to a counted night. The vessels from chapter 1 have come home as evidence.

loadBearing.plain: Three market-words on the wall: MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN — numbered, weighed, divided. This is an audit, not a ghost story.

links.because: Daniel reads the three verbs: the kingdom is finished, the king is too light, the realm is split to Medes and Persians.
Isaiah already named Cyrus and spoke of open gates. The plaster and the older prophet agree on the same night.

loadBearing.sitting: Gold ends on a written scale. Every later metal can be numbered, weighed, and replaced the same way.

loadBearing.plain: God calls Cyrus by name long before this feast and says he will open gates before him. The conqueror is already on the page.

links.because: PERES: the kingdom is given to the Medes and Persians — Cyrus’s people.
That same night Belshazzar is killed and a new ruler receives the city. Isaiah’s open gates meet Daniel’s writing.

loadBearing.sitting: The fall is not a lucky siege. A named king and a written audit arrive together.

loadBearing.plain: In that night Belshazzar is slain. The gold kingdom does not fade over decades on this page; it ends before morning.

links.because: The dream already said another kingdom would arise after Babylon. Silver has arrived on schedule.
Chapter 7 will draw that second kingdom as a bear. One night, two pictures: metal and beast.

loadBearing.sitting: Silver takes gold exactly when the dream said another kingdom would arise.

6.title: Daniel 6
6.kicker: Aramaic · the law that could not be changed
6.jumpLabel: The unchangeable decree and the open window

marks.phrase: the law of the Medes and Persians

loadBearing.plain: The satraps search Daniel’s record and find no corruption. Their only hope is to attack the law of his God.

links.because: The same man who drew a line at the king’s table now draws it at an open window. Worship is still the test.
His three friends already said “but if not.” The den is their furnace in Persian clothes.

loadBearing.sitting: Faithfulness has become the indictment. The charge is not fraud. It is prayer.

loadBearing.plain: Medo-Persian law, once signed, cannot be repealed — even by the king who signed it. That rigidity is the trap.

links.because: Esther’s book uses the same pride: a royal word that cannot be altered. This is how the silver kingdom likes to sound eternal.
Darius wants to save Daniel and cannot. Heaven will overrule the statute without rewriting it.

loadBearing.sitting: An unchangeable human law is still smaller than the first commandment.

loadBearing.plain: Daniel hears the decree, goes home, and prays toward Jerusalem three times a day as before. He does not close the window.

links.because: Solomon already taught exiles to pray toward the city God chose. Daniel is keeping that old habit in public.
When human law criminalizes worship, the apostles name the same duty: obey God rather than men.

loadBearing.sitting: The sitting’s question is whether that habit exists on an ordinary Tuesday, before any den is opened.

loadBearing.plain: Peter and the apostles say it in one sentence: we ought to obey God rather than men. That is the civil limit Daniel already lived.

links.because: Open windows toward Jerusalem are that sentence in a daily schedule.
The furnace said the same limit when the music played. Two empires, one first commandment.

loadBearing.sitting: The den and the furnace teach one rule: no earthly statute can cancel worship of the Most High.

loadBearing.plain: Daniel says God sent his angel and shut the lions’ mouths. He was innocent before God and before the king.

links.because: The fourth figure in the fire was the same kind of rescue: God present in the danger, not only after it.
Darius then writes that men must tremble before Daniel’s God — the living God who outlasts an unchangeable statute.

loadBearing.sitting: The living God outlasts a law that could not be changed. The window was the victory; the dawn only showed it.

7.title: Daniel 7
7.kicker: Aramaic · beasts, horn, and the heavenly court, 553 B.C.
7.jumpLabel: The four beasts and the court

marks.phrase: a time and times and the dividing of time

loadBearing.plain: The first beast is a lion with eagle’s wings. Then the wings are plucked and it is given a man’s heart. This is Babylon again.

links.because: The head of gold was already named Babylon. The lion is that same first kingdom in beast-language.
Nebuchadnezzar’s mind was changed to a beast’s, then restored. “A man’s heart” here remembers that sermon.

loadBearing.sitting: Gold and lion are one empire. Chapter 7 is not a new chain. It is the same chain with teeth.

loadBearing.plain: Among ten horns a smaller horn comes up, pulls up three, and has eyes and a mouth speaking great things. This is a different kind of power among Rome’s pieces.

links.because: The angel’s job description: diverse from the ten, wears out saints, changes times and laws, lasts a time, times, and dividing of time.
John sees a mouth speaking great things given forty-two months — the same measured boast in another book.

loadBearing.sitting: The horn rises among the ten, not from a fourth metal outside the statue. Use the checklist. Do not pick a favorite villain first.

loadBearing.plain: Thrones are set in heaven, the Ancient of Days sits, books are opened. This court meets while the horn is still active on earth.

links.because: One like a son of man is brought to the Ancient of Days to receive the forever kingdom. He comes to heaven first, not yet to earth as in chapter 2’s stone-strike.
The same court then takes the horn’s dominion away. Judgment sits before the kingdom is given to the saints.

loadBearing.sitting: The court sits in heaven before the stone strikes the earth. Do not collapse 7:9–14 into the Second Coming scene of 2:44.

loadBearing.plain: The horn thinks to change times and laws and is given a measured season: a time (1) + times (2) + a dividing of time (½) = 3½ years.

links.because: Forty-two months is the same 3½ years written another way (42 × 30 days = 1,260 days).
A time, times, and a half appears again at the book’s end. Same riddle-phrase, same measured span.

loadBearing.sitting: Build 1,260 days from the riddle first. Then the year-day scale turns those days into years. 538–1798 is a test, not a magic label.

loadBearing.plain: John is shown a beast given a mouth speaking great things, and power for forty-two months. Scripture itself equates Daniel’s riddle with 1,260 days.

links.because: The mouth speaking great things is already in Daniel. John is not inventing a new villain.
Time, times, and dividing = 3½ = 42 months = 1,260 days. Three writings, one span.

loadBearing.sitting: You do not need a preacher to invent 1,260. Revelation writes the arithmetic next to Daniel’s mouth.

8.title: Daniel 8
8.jumpLabel: The ram, the goat, and the sanctuary

loadBearing.plain: Daniel sees a ram with two horns; one horn is higher and came up last. You do not have to guess the empire. The angel will name it.

links.because: Gabriel says it in plain speech: the ram is the kings of Media and Persia.
The bear raised on one side was already that uneven pair. Ram and bear are the silver kingdom twice.

loadBearing.sitting: Media and Persia are named before anyone argues. Start here, then watch the goat.

loadBearing.plain: The goat’s great horn is broken at the height of its power, and four horns come up toward the four winds. One empire becomes four.

links.because: The goat is Grecia; the great horn is the first king (Alexander); the four are four kingdoms that stand up after him.
The leopard’s four heads were already those four. Greece is named; the Diadochi are the four winds.

loadBearing.sitting: Alexander dies; four generals divide. The next horn must rise from this Greek settlement, not from a guess.

loadBearing.plain: A holy one asks how long the attack on the sanctuary lasts. The answer is 2,300 evenings-mornings; then the sanctuary is nitsdaq — put right, justified — not merely mopped.

links.because: Gabriel will cut seventy weeks from this longer line so the cross can date it. Chapter 9 is the key that unlocks 8:14.
Israel already knew a day when the sanctuary was put right: the Day of Atonement. That is the older grammar for this verse.

loadBearing.sitting: If these were ordinary days, 2,300 days is about six years — and Antiochus’s crisis lasted about three. The unit is the year-day ruler from sitting 0.

loadBearing.plain: On the Day of Atonement the high priest entered the Most Holy Place so Israel could be clean before the Lord. That is what “sanctuary put right” already meant.

links.because: Nitsdaq points to that day’s work, not to a janitor’s mop in 164 B.C.
The heavenly court that sits and opens books is the same judgment scene this Day of Atonement was picturing.

loadBearing.sitting: Learn Leviticus 16 here so 1844 is not a slogan. Cleansing has a calendar and a room in Scripture already.

loadBearing.plain: Gabriel says twice that this vision belongs to the time of the end. A second-century cleanup cannot use up a line aimed past the prophet’s own horizon.

links.because: He says it again: “at the time of the end shall be the vision.” The sitting is not allowed to park the whole chapter in 164 B.C.
The vision of evenings-mornings is true, and it is for many days. “Many days” is the hint to keep the long ruler.

loadBearing.sitting: Antiochus is too small and too early. The angel’s own horizon — the time of the end — is why.

9.title: Daniel 9
9.kicker: Hebrew · seventy weeks cut off from the 2,300

loadBearing.plain: Gabriel says seventy weeks are determined (chathak — cut off) for Daniel’s people. He is not starting a new clock from zero. He is cutting a piece from a longer line.

links.because: Daniel had fainted because no one could explain the 2,300-day vision. Gabriel now returns to “the vision.”
The only long unexplained span on the table is those 2,300 evenings-mornings. The seventy weeks are cut from that.

loadBearing.sitting: Ask “cut off from what?” The answer is the 2,300. That is why chapter 9 can date chapter 8.

loadBearing.plain: In the seventh year of Artaxerxes, Ezra goes up from Babylon. This study reads that year as 457 B.C. — the start of the seventy weeks.

links.because: The clock starts at a word “to restore and to build Jerusalem.” Ezra 7 is the decree that restores magistrates, not only stones.
The decree itself: whoever will, go up to Jerusalem. Restoration is civic and liturgical.

loadBearing.sitting: Work 457 + 483 on paper (no year 0). You should see A.D. 27, the anointing of Jesus, with your own arithmetic.

loadBearing.plain: Artaxerxes writes: any of God’s people who wish may go to Jerusalem. This is a royal permit to restore the community, not only to stack bricks.

links.because: The date stamp is the king’s seventh year. That is why 457 B.C. is on the chart.
“Restore and build” needs government as well as walls. Ezra 7:25–26 even appoints magistrates and judges.

loadBearing.sitting: Cyrus rebuilt the temple; Nehemiah later repaired walls. This sitting picks 457 because it is the first decree that matches “restore” as rule.

loadBearing.plain: After the sixty-two weeks, Messiah is cut off, but not for himself. That is Jesus dying for others, not a later tyrant inserted after a gap.

links.because: The “he” who confirms the covenant for one week continues this same Messiah. In the middle of the week sacrifice ends — the cross.
Isaiah already said he was cut off from the land of the living for the transgression of the people. Daniel uses the same cut.

loadBearing.sitting: The seventieth week is not a future seven-year pause. The week that lands on Messiah is the Bible’s proof that the days were years.

loadBearing.plain: If 490 years are cut from 2,300, 1,810 years remain after A.D. 34. That leftover lands in 1844 on the same line the cross already sealed.

links.because: The cut, the decree, and the midst of the week are why 8:14 is no longer a floating number.
Sanctuary putting-right belongs to the Day of Atonement. In 1844 that day fell on 22 October by the Karaite new-moon count.

loadBearing.sitting: If Messiah died on schedule, the leftover sanctuary years sit on the same cord. That is the sitting’s load-bearing claim.

10.title: Daniel 10–12
10.kicker: Hebrew · princes, close of probation, resurrection

marks.phrase: prince of the kingdom of Persia

loadBearing.plain: The messenger was delayed twenty-one days by the “prince of Persia” until Michael came to help. Behind the silver kingdom is an unseen war, not only a king’s court.

links.because: Michael is called “your prince” — the great prince who stands for Daniel’s people.
That same Michael will stand up at the end. The last sitting begins with a Person, not a new empire.

loadBearing.sitting: The metals were never only geology. Nations move because princes wrestle, then because kings sign.

loadBearing.plain: A power takes away the daily (tamid) and sets up an abomination. Chapter 11 is marching the same sanctuary-attack onto a longer field.

links.because: The little horn already removed the tamid and cast down the sanctuary. This is that war continued, not a new subject.
The 1,290 days are counted from “the time that the daily shall be taken away.” Chapter 12 uses this same daily.

loadBearing.sitting: Watch the daily. The last numbers in the book start from this removal, on the same year-day ruler.

loadBearing.plain: Michael stands up, and there is a time of trouble such as never was. In sanctuary language a priest sits while he ministers and stands when that work is finished.

links.because: Michael is already “your prince.” This study reads him as Christ, the great prince of the host.
The court that sat and opened books is the judgment this standing closes. Advocacy ends; verdict and trouble follow.

loadBearing.sitting: “Stand up” is not a general putting on a helmet. It is the close of priestly plea. You may test the name; do not empty the sanctuary picture.

loadBearing.plain: Many who sleep in the dust of the earth will wake: some to everlasting life, some to shame. This is a body rising, not a mood and not reincarnation.

links.because: Isaiah already said the dead shall live and the earth shall cast out the dead. Daniel says it in court-clear words.
Jesus uses the same two-way rising: life and damnation. The New Testament is not adding a new hope; it is naming this one.

loadBearing.sitting: The book’s last hope is a body, not a chart. Empires end; dust-sleepers wake.

loadBearing.plain: God tells aged Daniel to go his way, rest (die), and stand in his lot at the end of the days. The prophet himself is promised a place in that rising.

links.because: The trouble, the book of names, and the dust-waking are the scene he will join.
The book is sealed till the time of the end. Daniel can rest without having to finish every chart in his own lifetime.

loadBearing.sitting: The sealed book ends on a name and a rising. The metals, beasts, horns, and numbers were always walking toward this sentence.
